title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra for computer-use workloads
dek: A lower-priced model prioritizes visual understanding and tool-driven desktop tasks over frontier reasoning per token.
evidence: OpenAI vendor benchmark and price disclosures, not an independent ranking
takeaway: Compare cost and successful completion across identical computer-use tasks before substituting a cheaper model.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Desktop agents spend tokens on interpreting screens, planning and retries. Cost per useful completed workflow matters more than token price alone.

paragraphs: Agent costs multiply: Desktop agents spend tokens on interpreting screens, planning and retries. Cost per useful completed workflow matters more than token price alone.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: OpenAI positions GPT-6.1 Terra for visual reasoning, form and application interaction, diagram interpretation and natural writing across API, Work and Codex.
Standard API text pricing is $1/M input, $0.05/M cached input and $5/M output tokens; tools and other modalities may have separate charges.

paragraphs: Computer-use specialization: OpenAI positions GPT-6.1 Terra for visual reasoning, form and application interaction, diagram interpretation and natural writing across API, Work and Codex.
Pricing: Standard API text pricing is $1/M input, $0.05/M cached input and $5/M output tokens; tools and other modalities may have separate charges.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: At medium effort on Agents' Last Exam, OpenAI reports a 15-percentage-point gain over GPT-5.6 Terra at about one-third the cost.
The release announcement is a vendor evaluation; task complexity, retries, tools, thinking effort and app latency alter realized cost and success.

paragraphs: Task-level vendor comparison: At medium effort on Agents' Last Exam, OpenAI reports a 15-percentage-point gain over GPT-5.6 Terra at about one-third the cost.
Limits: The release announcement is a vendor evaluation; task complexity, retries, tools, thinking effort and app latency alter realized cost and success.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Compare like-for-like screen navigation, data-entry, error recovery and complex multi-app work with the same tools and success rubric.
Track cost per successful action and p95 completion time, including failed attempts—not just nominal $/million tokens.

paragraphs: Evaluate verified task success: Compare like-for-like screen navigation, data-entry, error recovery and complex multi-app work with the same tools and success rubric.
Price the entire loop: Track cost per successful action and p95 completion time, including failed attempts—not just nominal $/million tokens.
